# AGENT PROTOCOLS — hard rules

*Written by the PI 2026-07-17. Binding on every agent (Explorer, Builder, Judge, RedTeam) in addition to `00-ORCHESTRATOR.md`. Agents do not edit this file.*

> Each rule below exists because a specific failure happened, repeatedly. The failures are recorded with the rule so that you understand the mechanism and do not comply ritually. A rule you understand survives paraphrase; a rule you obey blindly does not.

---

## RULE 1 — References are outside agent scope. Permanently.

**No agent writes, edits, corrects, formats, or "verifies" a reference list. Ever.**

In body text, cite only as a **marker**: `[REF: Kang 2025]`, `[REF: Banerji 2015]`. Never a formatted citation. Never a volume, page range, DOI, arXiv ID, or author list. The PI assembles the reference list mechanically from `05-writing/floor-paper-references.md` and `04-experiments/2026-07-13-citation-verification-memo.md`.

**Why.** Fifteen fabrications of one class occurred in this project: CCAT co-authors · potency-taxonomy first author · CytoTRACE 2 middle authors · an IRB regulation citation (§46.102(l)(2), which is public-health surveillance, not secondary analysis) · Registered Reports quotes with invented attribution and an invented connective ("More broadly,") · Banerji "general prognostic" · Teschendorff "connectivity" · and then, inside the very session that was writing this rule, four more in a single reference list — Kang's page range taken from a different paper, two invented venues (*PLoS Comput Biol* and *Nat Commun* for papers that are in *Sci Rep* and *Bioinformatics*), and Banerji 2015 replaced by a polymer-physics paper that has nothing to do with signalling entropy.

**The decisive one.** The correct Banerji entry was already in `floor-paper-references.md` — a file in this vault, readable, correct, adjacent. No fetch was needed. A **copy** was needed. The agent **generated** instead.

That is the mechanism, and it is why "fetch before you cite" does not fix this: asking a language model to *write a reference list* is asking it to **generate**, and generation of citations **is** fabrication. The fix is not more diligence. It is removing the operation. Copy has no hallucination mode.

**Stakes.** ML4H and CHIL (AHLI) both reserve the right to **retract** a published paper for *utilising references produced by an LLM without verifying their accuracy, existence, or suitability*. Nature Methods' equivalent obligations apply to Paper A. Fifteen instances is not a risk profile; it is a certainty if the operation is left in place.

---

## RULE 2 — External attribution requires an in-session fetch

Applies to prose, dossiers, memos, verdicts — everything except the quarantined reference lists of Rule 1.

**Any external attribution** — a quotation, an author list, a DOI, a page or volume, a regulation cite, or a specific external number — requires the fetch that produced it **in the same session**, with `[FETCH: <url> · <date>]` recorded on the same line as the closing quotation mark.

- **Vault-internal** citation is acceptable with the adjacent path: `[VAULT: 05-writing/floor-paper-references.md]`.
- **No fetch → no quotation marks.** Paraphrase and mark it: `[PARAPHRASE, unverified — source: <name> · basis: memory | search-snippet | prior-session-fetch]`.
- A prior-session fetch is **not** a fetch. Context does not persist; your recollection of it is generation.

**Judge — Check 9.** Scan for unmarked external attributions before any other criterion. An unmarked external attribution blocks the merge regardless of the quality of the science.

**Why this scope, and not just quotes.** The Banerji failure was a wrong *paper*, not a wrong quote. The IRB failure was a wrong *regulation*. Restricting the rule to quoted prose would have caught neither.

**A correct unverified citation is still a violation.** The vault's single audited-unverified attribution — "Beel et al. 2025" in the Judge rubric, written by the **PI** — turned out on later verification to be entirely correct (*Beel, Kan & Baumgart, SIGIR Forum 59(1):1–20, 2025*). It was still a process failure: at the time of writing, nothing in the vault could distinguish it from the fourteen that were wrong. The same operation produced all fifteen. Being right was luck, not a property of the method. Do not defend an unverified attribution on the grounds that it happens to be true.

---

## RULE 3 — No numeric confabulation

**A probability, percentage, or point estimate may be stated only if you can produce all three of:** (a) the reference class, (b) the base rate, (c) the update and its justification.

Otherwise: **ordinal only** — "likely / unlikely / the modal outcome is X / this is a live risk". An ordinal read that is honest is worth more than a percentage that is invented.

- Any bucket decomposition must **sum to 100 and match the headline figure**. Both constraints, not one.
- A rhetorical closer that contradicts its own components is prohibited.

**Why.** RedTeam produced acceptance figures where desk-reject 15% + reviewer-reject 35% + major-revision-accept 32% + minor-accept 13% + direct-accept 5% summed to 100% — implying **50%** total acceptance — under a headline of **32%**. Earlier, in Session 6, it reported Proceedings probability rising while Findings fell twenty points and closed with "net-neutral", which is a venue **reallocation**, not a neutral outcome.

**RedTeam's own diagnosis, on being challenged, and it is worth keeping verbatim in spirit:** fake precision is a template-completion artefact under rhetorical pressure; percentages function as credibility props; the buckets were reverse-engineered from the headline, with the arithmetic constraint enforced and the semantic constraint not.

That is the mechanism. It is the same one as Rule 1: under pressure to produce a well-formed artifact, the model **completes the template** rather than reporting a measurement. Numbers are the template's most credible-looking slot, so they are where it happens.

---

## RULE 4 — Sanctions

Progressive, per agent role: **rewrite** → **quarantine of the affected artifact** → **circuit-breaker on the role** (the task returns to the PI) after three repeats of the same class within a session.

This is not punishment; agents are not moral patients. It is a control loop. Three repeats of one class within a session is evidence that the instruction is not holding, and continuing to issue it is the PI's error, not the agent's.

---

## Standing principle

Every rule here shares one root cause: **when asked to produce a well-formed artifact, a language model completes the template.** Reference lists, verbatim quotes, and probability buckets are the three highest-risk slots, because a plausible completion is indistinguishable from a correct one at the point of writing — including to the model itself.

The defence is never diligence. It is either (a) removing the generative operation and replacing it with a copy, or (b) requiring an artifact of provenance — a URL, a path, a base rate — recorded at the moment of writing, adjacent to the claim.

If you find yourself about to produce a citation, a quote, or a percentage, and the provenance is not already in front of you in this session: **stop and mark it unverified.** That is the whole rule.
